task.text:
Hi Kenji,

Option 1 is clearly my favorite, and this is unquestionably the closest we’ve come so far. For the first time, I feel that we’re closing in on the answer instead of still searching for it.

The major breakthrough is that I’ve stopped judging the two arms separately. The left arm has finally become quiet enough to support the overall composition, while the right arm is starting to show the personality I’ve been seeking.

Rather than adding any new ideas, the next refinement should make the whole V feel inevitable. I don’t want my reaction to be “interesting left arm” or “beautiful right arm”; I want to perceive a single, complete letter.

Without gaining weight, the right arm could still acquire slightly more presence and confidence. It should seem to rise with purpose, not merely flow with motion. Some movement is beautiful, but the movement itself must not become the defining feature. There is also room to make both arms feel inherently related, rather than like two independent gestures that happen to meet at one point.

Reading your notes also clarified something for me: “modern” isn’t really the quality I’m after. The goal is timelessness—a form that seems as though it has always existed and always will. It should feel confident, enduring, and authoritative, never contemporary or driven by trends. Above all, the V should feel inevitable.

We’re very close now, and I’m genuinely excited to keep refining this family.
